extracted.intended_audience: mathematicians, math educators, and authors of mathematical proofs (proof-writers and researchers in mathematical practice)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for composing published mathematical proofs so they support how mathematicians actually read: skimmable global structure, accessible local detail, and cues that enable reuse, heuristics extraction, and plan reconstruction.

rubrics_metrics.name: States its main idea clearly
rubrics_metrics.description: The proof 'states its main idea clearly' at the top so readers can extract the core insight.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Helps readers gain 'understanding the main idea'; avoid hiding the main idea midstream. A clear top-level statement of the key idea allows readers to skim and form a global picture before zooming into details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Names the technique explicitly
rubrics_metrics.description: The proof 'names its technique' (identifies the method being used).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Helps 'understanding the technique' and lets readers recognize reusable methods. If a standard method is being used, label it; if novel, summarize its distinctive features so readers can compare to alternatives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Highlights reusable lemmas / intermediate results
rubrics_metrics.description: The proof 'highlights reusable lemmas' or intermediate results that may be useful elsewhere.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make lemmas explicit and clearly stated (with names/labels) so readers can spot components they might reuse, instead of burying them inside long calculations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Marks the load-bearing (critical) step(s)
rubrics_metrics.description: The proof 'marks the load-bearing step' — identifies where the real difficulty lies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicitly signal which step(s) are critical; indicate which arguments are routine versus which contain the novel idea or hardest work. This supports readers' local attention and verification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acknowledges alternatives and compares approaches
rubrics_metrics.description: The proof 'acknowledges alternatives' and, where appropriate, compares the presented proof to other known approaches.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Briefly note how the method differs from or relates to other proofs; this facilitates readers' comparative evaluation and learning about trade-offs between approaches.

rubrics_metrics.name: Extracts and states heuristic principles
rubrics_metrics.description: The proof 'extracts the heuristic principle' or general strategy embodied by the argument.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State the guiding heuristic or intuition behind steps so readers can generalize the approach to new problems; include informal commentary or remarks that communicate the 'why' behind choices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Discusses extensions, limitations, and applicability
rubrics_metrics.description: The proof 'discusses extensions and limits' — what generalizations or constraints apply to the method.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Indicate domains where the technique may or may not work, possible extensions, and natural next problems. This supports the reader goal of 'adapting to new problems.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Has clear modular structure
rubrics_metrics.description: The proof 'has clear modular structure' so sections can be treated as black boxes (modular reading).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Organize the proof into labeled lemmas/claims/sections with clear purposes so readers can verify section-level correctness without reading every detail; modular structure supports skimming and selective zooming.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provides scannable section headings and signposts
rubrics_metrics.description: The proof 'has scannable section headings and signposts' to support global skimming.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use informative headings, 'roadmap' paragraphs, and explicit signposting language (e.g. 'We now reduce to...', 'The key lemma is...') so readers can form a quick global map and navigate to interesting parts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Includes worked examples or illustrative remarks
rubrics_metrics.description: The proof 'has worked-example sections or remarks' showing how steps apply to concrete examples.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide examples, special cases, or remarks that demonstrate the method in action; helps readers test understanding and 'study how steps apply to specific examples they have in mind.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Supports global ↔ local oscillation (skimmable + zoomable)
rubrics_metrics.description: The proof supports the empirical 'global ↔ local oscillation' reading style by being skimmable at a high level and providing richly accessible local detail when readers zoom in.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Score higher if the proof allows rapid switching between overview and detailed inspection: offer summaries, pointers to detailed proofs, and locally-dense accounts at critical steps; avoid forcing strictly linear, line-by-line reading.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provides detail-rich accounts at points readers will zoom into
rubrics_metrics.description: The proof is 'detail-rich' at the points where readers are likely to inspect steps more carefully.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include full justification or references for non-routine steps, and consider leaving routine computations concise; concentrate detailed derivations where the argument's novelty or fragility lies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Is honest about which sections are routine vs. critical
rubrics_metrics.description: The proof 'is honest about which sections are routine' and which carry the novel argument.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicitly label routine computations as such or cite standard results instead of expanding them unnecessarily; this prevents 'homogeneous detail' that hides significance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Enables plan reconstruction
rubrics_metrics.description: The proof facilitates the reader's ability to reconstruct the argument's plan (plan-recovery).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide a roadmap or outline of the proof strategy, state intermediate goals, and indicate how lemmas fit together so readers can rebuild the argument's structure rather than get lost in details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accommodates multiple reader strategies (authority, line-by-line, modular)
rubrics_metrics.description: The proof should be usable by readers who rely on author/journal authority, those who read line-by-line, and those who read modularly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognize that readers adopt different strategies; therefore include enough self-contained information for skeptical or less-known-author readers, while maintaining concise signals that satisfy readers who skim or treat sections as black boxes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supports non-deductive reasoning modes (analogy, plausibility)
rubrics_metrics.description: The proof 'engages in non-deductive reasoning' (analogy, plausibility arguments, 'this should work because...') to aid comprehension.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include analogies, plausibility checks, and intuitive commentary to supplement formal derivations; these aid readers' heuristic sense-making even when not strictly deductive.

rubrics_metrics.name: Is skim-friendly at the headline/section level
rubrics_metrics.description: The proof is 'skim-friendly' — at the section/headline level readers can form a useful impression without reading details.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use short descriptive headings, opening summaries, and explicit statements of purpose for sections so skimming yields substantive information (not just filler).

rubrics_metrics.name: Provides concrete applications or example applications
rubrics_metrics.description: The proof 'has example applications' or demonstrates how the method applies to problems of interest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include explicit applications, corollaries, or worked-out special cases that show the method's utility; these help readers evaluate reusability and adaptivity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Signals provenance and leverages/addresses authorial reputation
rubrics_metrics.description: The proof acknowledges the role of author/journal reputation: proofs from well-known authors may be trusted more, while proofs from unknown authors should be more self-supporting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For less-established authors, be especially explicit and self-contained; for established authors, don't rely solely on reputation—still provide signposts and clarity. The community's trust distribution is an empirical factor in reading and should inform presentation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoids hiding the main idea in midstream (anti-pattern)
rubrics_metrics.description: Anti-pattern: the proof 'hides the main idea in midstream', making it hard for readers to extract the core insight.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not bury the main idea deep inside technical calculations; surface it early and restate it when appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoids homogeneous detail throughout (anti-pattern)
rubrics_metrics.description: Anti-pattern: 'homogeneous detail throughout' that prevents readers from discerning which parts matter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Differentiate routine from critical sections; vary granularity so readers can prioritize their attention instead of being forced into exhaustive line-by-line checking.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoids lack of signposts (anti-pattern)
rubrics_metrics.description: Anti-pattern: 'no signposts' prevents effective skimming and navigation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide headings, roadmaps, and explicit transitions; without signposts readers cannot form a global map or quickly find critical parts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoids providing no examples (anti-pattern)
rubrics_metrics.description: Anti-pattern: 'no example applications' denies readers the ability to test and internalize the method.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include illustrative examples or remarks demonstrating the technique; absence of examples reduces the proof's pedagogical and heuristic value.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoids misleading section structure (anti-pattern)
rubrics_metrics.description: Anti-pattern: 'misleading section structure' where modular reading gives a false picture.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure section boundaries reflect genuine modular decomposition; don't structure sections in a way that suggests independence when details are scattered or interdependent.
